cleared.check: Static census of every inlined journal checkpoint in eight shipped reth-derived binaries (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.8.1, Base v1.5.6, world-chain v2.8.2, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, celo-reth v1.0.10, xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1, arc-execution v0.8.6): every place that raises the depth word J+0x118 and saves the three journal lengths, found by byte pattern and read in objdump text (scan.py, classify.py).
cleared.result: Accepted sites: celo 21 of 22, op-reth v2.10 56 of 60, op-reth v2.8.1 50 of 52, Base 229 of 234, World Chain 48 of 49, Zora 48 of 49, X Layer 18 of 18, Arc 25 of 40. Each accepted site loads logs J+0x10, journal J+0x28 and the third list J+0x40 from the same journal base as the out-of-line copy, stores them as one record in that order and raises the depth by exactly one, and every revert call after it in the same function passes that record. The sites not accepted were read by hand: op-reth make_call_frame 0x456e2d5 reloads the host pointer from [rsp+0x8] for each load and stores the record at rsp+0x238, which the revert at 0x456f364 receives; the 15 Arc sites in 0x295e140 and its copies keep journal_i in a register and copy the record to rsp+0x310 before the revert at 0x295eb06, in the right order; the rest have another depth offset and are not journal code.

cleared.check: Every saturating decrement of a depth word in the same eight binaries, run in a small interpreter of its own instructions for depth 0, 1, 2, 3, 1023, 1024, 1025, 2^63 and 2^64-1.
cleared.result: Celo 81 of 81, op-reth v2.10 63 of 63, v2.8.1 60 of 61, Base 137 of 181, World Chain 64 of 67, Zora 81 of 89, X Layer 47 of 47 and Arc 64 of 66 give max(d-1, 0). The two Base sites that differ decrement a stack loop counter at rsp+0x188 in allocator code. The uninterpreted sites lie in database, download and genesis code, or are an Arc pattern that raises and lowers the depth in one step and that the interpreter handles. The guard in front of the frame return commit compares the result byte with 4 on celo and Arc (revm-interpreter 35, no Suspend variant) and with 5 on the other builds (revm-interpreter 37 and 43, Suspend = 4), as return_ok! in each crate version says.

cleared.check: Task 3 on celo-reth v1.0.10: the commit_tx block inlined in CeloHandler::execution_result 0x1e9cbd0 (0x1e9e44c-0x1e9e639) and the discard path of CeloHandler::catch_error 0x1e94290 (full checkpoint_revert with a zero record, then the clear 0x1e94653-0x1e94840), run on journals with 1 to 40 writes, open frames up to depth 6, logs and list entries.
cleared.result: 1,000 commit and 1,000 discard cases (seeds 38211, 38212): afterwards the transient map holds no item, every one of 5,988 and 5,900 written transient words reads zero through the lifted TLOAD handler in the next transaction, depth 0, journal, logs and list empty, transaction id plus one. Five planted faults in commit_tx (keeps transient, journal, depth, transaction id, logs) were caught. A fault that skips the transient clear in the discard path is not observable, because the full revert before it already removes every transient word, and every TSTORE is journaled. After either path alloy-evm calls finalize, which clears logs, transient storage, journal and depth again and resets the id (revm-context 18.0.3 inner.rs finalize).

cleared.check: What a transient leak across transactions would hand the next transaction, read in src/.
cleared.result: unlock sets the flag, calls back, requires NonzeroDeltaCount to be zero and clears the flag before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, Lock.sol:10-21). A successful transaction therefore ends with the flag false and the count zero, and a reverted one is undone by the journal. Only the synced currency and reserves (CurrencyReserves.sol) can be left set by a successful transaction, which is the A1 case earlier cycles closed. No path between two transactions was found that skips the clear.

These networks run no reth-derived binary that earlier cycles identified (Nitro, bor and erigon, avalanchego, Monad, the closed MegaETH and HyperEVM nodes), so this lift does not apply to them. Their call frame and journal code was tested through source, RPC and other binaries in earlier cycles.

leadResults.answer: The frame code of celo-reth, xlayer-reth, arc-execution and op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 inlines the checkpoint and the commit and calls an out-of-line checkpoint_revert. The inlined blocks equal the out-of-line copies in field offsets and arithmetic, and ran from the binaries in 2,118 sequences per binary, with logs, with no mismatch. X Layer frame code calls a third revert copy 0x3ce8080 that had not run; it ran here without a difference. 20 planted faults were caught.

Celo commit_tx and discard paths ran from the binary on 2,000 populated journals and clear the transient map, depth, journal, logs and list and advance the id; finalize clears again. The other seven builds were located only in part and not run; op-reth discard_tx ran in cycle 37.

The branch was read: it tests a 32-bit word at State+0x78 and calls a lookup before the fallback read. It was not run. The access list comes from the block executor or the block, so an ordinary account cannot write it.
